- Gallery: the strip of small pictures under the viewer now keeps the current picture in its middle: you drag the strip and the big picture above changes with it, picture by picture, while the strip stays centred under it; when you let go it settles on a picture. It was slow: the strip's thumbnails are now the same ones the grid already made (no second set to read), the current one is shown bigger by scaling instead of changing its size, and while you run through the strip the big picture shows the small one at once and is read at full size only after a moment (not for every picture passed).
- Gallery: zooming in (two fingers or a double tap) hides the bars; bringing the picture back to the whole picture (a double tap, or pinching out) shows them again. A double tap on a zoomed picture zooms out.
- Gallery: "Delete this picture?" is now a small rounded card low on the screen, over the buttons (not a dialog in the middle of the picture), with Cancel and a red Delete; a tap outside or Back closes it.
- Gallery: videos are shown in the grid by default (the Videos switch is in the gallery settings) and a tap on one plays it in Pulse's own video player, over the gallery, instead of asking another app.
- The Photos app icon lost its outer frame: the picture mark (mountains and sun) is bigger, in the plain icon and the single-colour one.
- Builds: a release now also makes the Google Play bundle (Pulse-<version>-play.aab, the Play flavor with Pulse AI inside) next to the full and the lite APK. It is built beside them and never holds the release back: if it fails, the two APKs are still published.
- Gallery: Back on a picture opened from the gallery closes only the picture and leaves the gallery (its cover page) as it was; before, it left the whole Photos app.
- Gallery: the search now also finds pictures by what is in them, found on the phone itself (nothing is sent anywhere). The pictures are read in the background, newest first, and the result is kept (a picture is read once); the search page says how far it is. Type "kedi", "cat", "pizza", "kahve" or "stetoskop" and the pictures that show it come up (a word with one letter wrong, like "astetoskop", still finds it; so does the start of a word). It knows the 1000 things of the ImageNet list (animals and dog breeds, foods, vehicles, instruments, tools, clothes, places in nature...), and "hayvan", "yemek", "araç", "doğa", "meyve", "enstrüman" find a whole kind. The recogniser is EfficientNet-Lite0 (TensorFlow Lite, Apache 2.0, 5 MB, int8) and its names have Turkish words.
- Gallery: faces, simply: the pictures are looked at with Android's own face finder, and "yüz", "kişi", "insan", "portre" (or "face", "people") find the pictures with a face in them, "selfie" one big face, "grup" three or more. It does not tell people apart from each other (that needs a face-recognition model, which is not in yet).
- Gallery: a swipe up on a picture opens its details; the sheet slides up from the bottom and slides away again (a swipe down on the sheet or on the picture, the close button or Back closes it). A zoomed picture is moved by the fingers as before. The gallery settings got: Open in video player (off: another app is asked), Swipe up for details, Merge albums (off: albums with the same name in different folders stay apart, told apart by the folder above) next to the ones it had (live autoplay, film strip, zoom, confirm delete, keep the screen on, hidden albums ...).
- Keyboard: a word you took back from an automatic correction once is never corrected again, to the same word or to another (a swapped-letters word used to get a second chance, and a correction to a different word was not remembered).
- Keyboard: a bar that would stay empty now shows the last words you wrote (up to three), the common words of the language only filling what is missing; the bar is also made again whenever the keyboard window is shown again (back from a screenshot or another window), not only on the first key.
- Keyboard: e-mail addresses are remembered from what is copied too (an address pasted or filled in was never typed on the keyboard, so it was never kept), and Settings has a new "Your e-mail addresses" list to add one by hand (umut... then offers it in any field) and to remove one.
- Keyboard, Effects: every option now shows what it does: a small keyboard with the colour wash, a key with its colour effect, a key pressed over and over with its motion (the same press size and spring as the real key), and a speaker tile for the sounds (a tap plays it).
- Keyboard, Statistics: the "99% learned" ring was made up: four rings that were full after a few thousand words (3000 words, 400 typos, 30000 letters) averaged, so it read about 99 for everyone. It is gone. The ring now shows what is measured: how many automatic corrections were kept (every way a correction was taken back counts: the undo, a backspace into the word, a word retyped), with the corrections per 100 words, the number taken back, the words and slips it knows.
- Keyboard: sliding along the space bar moves the cursor more exactly: a letter per step of the finger for the first six letters (it stops where the finger is and never runs past a letter), the speed-up for a long slide is gentler (a 20-step slide crossed 60 letters, now about 28), and the cursor takes at most four letters in one step and catches up with the finger on the next. The Cursor sensitivity setting still scales it.
- Floating keyboard, written again: its handle is one line. A tap on it turns the line into an X (its two halves turn, an animation, no icon) and a tap on the X closes the keyboard; left alone for three seconds the X is a line again, and every opening starts with the line. A drag on the handle only moves the keyboard (a touch on the handle no longer closed it by itself). The small close icon beside the handle is gone.
- Floating keyboard: after it closed, the screen did not answer for a moment: the floating window is tall, and while it went away the system took its whole height as the keyboard's (the floating session had ended first). A keyboard that is not on the screen now takes no touch at all, and the tile's invisible window closes with it.
- Gallery, after Samsung's Gallery: the pictures open under a big title ("Pictures", with how many pictures and videos) in the free space above the grid, and the small title in the bar shows once it has scrolled away; the tiles are square with thin gaps; the bottom tabs show their names under the icons (Pictures, Albums, Favorites); the settings page is "Gallery settings" with its groups as rounded cards under small grey titles, always open (no chevrons), like Samsung's.
- Screen recorder, the floating bar: it moves wherever it is dragged from, the buttons too (a tap stays a tap), and let go while moving it glides on a little and slows down, never leaving the screen; its place is kept for the next recording (it was held at the top left, and only its thin edge dragged it). A grip shows where to hold it.
- Screen recorder, the pen: a tap still draws on the screen; holding the pen now opens its box: the pen, the marker, the highlighter (see-through) and the eraser, each shown as the stroke it makes, nine colours, three sizes, undo and clear. Each stroke keeps the tool and colour it was drawn with, the eraser takes away only the drawing, and the choice is kept. Fast strokes keep every point the finger passed.
- Music, Windows Media Player 12 look: the launcher crashed with "Padding must be non-negative" (Pulse 1.0.418, reported): the volume knob's place was the bar's width minus the knob times the volume, and that went below zero while the bar was being laid out (no width yet). The volume and position knobs now stay between the bar's ends whatever the width or the value.
